history.summary: The well-known Mahakaleshwar Shiva temple of Udaipur stands at the entrance of Rani Road, Ambamata, overlooking Fateh Sagar Lake, in a complex of about 3.5 acres with smaller shrines to Parvati, Annapurna, Surya and others. Local belief calls the black-stone shivling swayambhu (self-manifested) and says the Nath saint Guru Gorakhnath worshipped here; daily aartis centre on the Rudrabhishek. FLAG: identity disambiguated - this is the ~900-year-old Ambamata/Rani Road temple, NOT the Ujjain Mahakaleshwar Jyotirlinga; some travel pages wrongly list it among the 12 Jyotirlingas and give a contradictory '14th century built in Garuda form' claim, neither of which is accepted here. Mahashivratri is the grand annual festival. No duplicates of other CSV rows found.

name: Mahakaleshwar Temple
town_description: Udaipur, the 'City of Lakes' in southern Rajasthan, was founded as the capital of the Mewar kingdom by Maharana Udai Singh II in 1559. Set among the Aravalli hills around Lake Pichola and Fateh Sagar, it is one of India's most visited heritage cities, known for its palaces, temples and old-city lanes.

travel.airport: Maharana Pratap Airport (Udaipur), about 23 km east.
travel.railway: Udaipur City railway station, about 4 km away.
travel.road: At the entrance of Rani Road, Ambamata, reached by taxi or auto-rickshaw from the city centre; a pleasant lakeside walk from Fateh Sagar.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; Mahashivratri sees the largest crowds.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Wikipedia lists darshan at 4:00 AM (Mangala), midday and evening/night - exact current slots not consistently published, verify on arrival.
